Here’s a quick snapshot of what’s publicly available for the phrase **“Diagnostic AI 0F.”** (the search was run with the exact quotation you gave): | Source | What it is | Key points | |--------|------------|------------| | **Microsoft Research – “Sequential Diagnosis with Language Models”** | A benchmark & orchestrator (MAI‑Diagnostic Orchestrator, MAI‑DxO) that turns clinical case studies into iterative diagnostic dialogues. | • 304 NEJM‑CPC cases.
• Iterative “question‑asker → test‑selector → diagnosis” loop.
• When paired with OpenAI o3, MAI‑DxO reaches ~80 % diagnostic accuracy (vs ~20 % for general physicians) and cuts test‑costs by 20‑70 % .
• Model‑agnostic: works with OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, Grok, DeepSeek, Llama families. | | **Hugging Face – `drdai/diagnify-14b-v0.2-cot`** | DIAGNIFY, a 14‑B parameter clinical‑reasoning model using chain‑of‑thought prompting + retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG). | • Generates structured differentials (body‑system groupings, life‑threat flags, weighted likelihood).
• Internal benchmark reports near‑100 % accuracy, but the authors flag this as a *pre‑liminary, unreplicated* result and explicitly say the model **is not for clinical use**. | | **Hugging Face – `Henrychur/DiagAgent-8B`** | DiagAgent‑8B, an RL‑optimised diagnostic agent trained in the *DiagGym* simulated clinical environment. | • Multi‑turn RL (GRPO) that recommends tests, updates the working diagnosis, and stops when enough evidence is gathered.
• Reported diagnosis‑accuracy > 80 % across several model sizes (7 B‑14 B). | | **Hugging Face – `FreedomIntelligence/DiagnosisGPT-6B`** | DiagnosisGPT‑6B, a general‑purpose medical LLM aimed at diagnostic assistance. | • Released as a research artifact; no detailed performance numbers in the snippet, but it’s part of the same family of “diagnostic‑AI” models. | | **Hugging Face – `heuristixai/HAI‑DiffDx‑0.5B`** | HAI‑DiffDx‑0.5B, a tiny (0.5 B) QLoRA‑fine‑tuned model that outputs a *four‑tier* differential (most likely, possible, unlikely‑but‑serious, recommended work‑up). | • Meant for research only; schema‑adherence on a tiny test set was ~56 % vs 4 % for the base model. | | **Other miscellaneous hits** | Various other medical‑AI repos and papers. | • Most are framed as “research‑only” or “decision‑support” tools, not cleared medical devices. | ### What this means for you - **“Diagnostic AI 0F”** does not appear to be a single, well‑known product or version number. The search results are a collection of recent research prototypes and open‑source LLM‑based diagnostic assistants. - If you were looking for a **specific commercial product** (e.g., a particular version number, a company’s “0F” release), the current public data don’t match that label. - If you need **details on a particular model** (e.g., DIAGNIFY, DiagAgent, DiagnosisGPT), I can pull the full technical report, model card, or evaluation metrics from the relevant Hugging Face page. - If you have a **use‑case in mind** (e.g., “I want a model that can iteratively ask questions and order tests”), let me know and I can point you at the most suitable open‑source option or summarize the Microsoft MAI‑DxO orchestrator design. **Next step:** Tell me which of the above you’re interested in (or clarify what “0F” refers to), and I’ll fetch the exact docs, performance numbers, or code you need.
